---
title: "Columns"
subtitle: "Labelling, aligning, sizing, hiding, moving, and combining columns."
description: "Keisen's column directives: columns-label, columns-align, columns-width, columns-hide, columns-move, and columns-combine."
---

| Function | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `columns-label(..pairs)` | Named arguments map a column name to its label. Labelling the row-name column labels the stubhead. |
| `columns-align(alignment, columns: auto)` | Sets alignment, direction-relative (`start`, `end`) or absolute. |
| `columns-width(widths)` | A dictionary of column name to length, fraction, or `auto`. |
| `columns-hide(..columns)` | Removes columns from the table; they stay readable by predicates and formatters. |
| `columns-move(..columns, before: none, after: none)` | Reorders columns relative to another column. |
| `columns-combine(into, from, pattern, label: auto, hide-sources: true)` | Builds one column from several. `pattern` takes one argument per source, in `from` order. |

: Column directives {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[45,55]"}

`columns-combine` receives the **formatted** content of its sources, not their raw values, which is what makes `(estimate, error) => [#estimate (#error)]` read the way it is written: each source keeps whatever its own `format-*` directive gave it.
The combined column takes the place of the first of its sources, and the sources are hidden rather than dropped, so predicates and formatters can still read them; `hide-sources: false` shows them as well.

A combined column is opaque afterwards, and that is the price of the pattern being free-form.
It carries content rather than alignment slots, so it is not decimal-aligned; it infers start alignment, so give it `columns-align(end, columns: ..)` when it holds figures; and it cannot be summarised, since content has no total.

There is no `columns-show`, and the asymmetry is deliberate.
Directives are the document's own, so a column is shown by not hiding it; an unhide exists only to undo a sibling directive a few lines above, which is ceremony rather than a feature.
A column named by no `columns-hide` is visible already.
